sentences.t: Val yd oed Wydyon diwarnawt yn y wely, ac yn deffroi, ef a glywei diaspat yn y gist is y draet.
sentences.l: As he-was Gwydion one-day in his bed, and waking, he it-was-that heard a-cry in the chest below his feet.
sentences.i: As Gwydion lay in his bed one day, waking, he heard a cry from the chest at his feet.
sentences.n: The part begins at col. 94 l. 10, on the line where the last part ended. Val 'as, while' (later fal, fel); yd oed 'was', with the particle yd before a vowel. Wydyon ← Gwydyon, softened after oed, as a noun often is straight after a form of bot. diwarnawt 'one day' (diwrnawt; diwyrnawt below). y wely ← gwely, softened after y 'his'. ef a glywei 'he heard' is the ordinary order of the tale's narrative: the subject first, then the particle a, then the verb, without any stress on the subject (the 'abnormal sentence'; l shows it as 'it-was-that'). glywei ← clywei, the imperfect of clywet, softened after a. diaspat 'cry, shriek'. y gist ← kist 'chest', softened after the article (kist is feminine). is 'below'. y draet ← traet 'feet', softened after y 'his'. This is the small chest at the foot of the bed in which Gwydion hid the 'little thing' at the end of the last part.

sentences.t: Kyny bei uchel hi, kyuuch oed ac y kigleu ef.
sentences.l: Though-it-might-not-be loud it, as-loud it-was as that heard he.
sentences.i: Though it was not loud, it was loud enough for him to hear.
sentences.n: Kyny 'though not': kyn 'though' + ny. bei, the imperfect subjunctive of bot, after kyn. hi 'it': diaspat is feminine. kyuuch 'as high, as loud', the equative of uchel; kyuuch … ac y 'as loud as that', that is, loud enough that. kigleu 'heard', an old 3 sg. preterite of clywet that has since vanished (later clywodd).

sentences.t: Sef a oruc ynteu, kyuodi yn gyflym, ac agori y gist.
sentences.l: That-is what he-did he-for-his-part: rising quickly, and opening the chest.
sentences.i: He rose quickly and opened the chest.
sentences.n: Sef 'that is (this)' introduces the answer to an implied question, what did he do?, and the answer is the verbal nouns kyuodi 'rising' and agori 'opening'. a oruc 'did', the preterite of gwneuthur. ynteu 'he for his part'. yn gyflym ← kyflym 'quick', softened after the adverbial yn. y gist ← kist, as before.

sentences.t: Ac ual y hegyr, ef a welei uab bychan yn rwyuaw y ureicheu o blyc y llen, ac yn y guascaru.
sentences.l: And as he-opens-it, he it-was-that saw a-boy little working his arms from the fold of the sheet, and its scattering.
sentences.i: And as he opened it, he saw a little boy working his arms out of the folds of the sheet and pushing it apart.
sentences.n: ual y hegyr 'as he opens it': hegyr is egyr, the 3 sg. present of agori, used in the past narrative for a vivid moment; the h- before it is the trace of an object pronoun 'it' (the chest, kist being feminine) after the particle y. uab ← mab, softened as the object. bychan 'little'. yn rwyuaw 'rowing, tossing', moving his arms as if rowing. y ureicheu ← breicheu 'arms', softened after y 'his'. o blyc ← plyc 'fold', softened after o. y llen 'the sheet': the brocade sheet Gwydion wrapped round the thing; llen is feminine, but ll (like rh) is not softened after the article. yn y guascaru 'in its scattering': guascaru (gwasgaru) 'spread out, scatter'. The g is not softened, so y here is not the masculine 'his'; it is either 'her, it' (the sheet) or y for eu 'their' (the arms), and either reading is possible.

sentences.t: Ac ef a gymerth y mab y rwng y dwylaw ac a gyrchwys y dref ac ef, lle y gwydat bot gwreic a bronneu genti.
sentences.l: And he it-was-that took the boy between his two-hands and that made-for the town with him, where he-knew there-being a-woman with breasts with-her.
sentences.i: And he took the boy in his hands and made for the town with him, to a place where he knew there was a woman nursing.
sentences.n: a gymerth ← kymerth 'took', the preterite of kymryt, softened after a. y rwng 'between'. y dwylaw 'his two hands' (dwy 'two' + llaw 'hand', softened in the compound). a gyrchwys ← kyrchwys 'made for', 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of kyrchu, softened after a. y dref ← tref 'town', softened after the article (tref is feminine), the object of kyrchu. ac ef 'with him': a 'with', ac before a vowel. lle y gwydat 'where he knew': gwydat, the imperfect of gwybot. bot 'being': 'that there was'. gwreic a bronneu genti 'a woman with breasts with her', that is, a woman in milk. genti 'with her', gan conjugated (3 sg. fem.).

sentences.t: Ac ymobryn a wnaeth a'r wreic ueithryn y mab.
sentences.l: And bargaining he-did with the woman to-rear the boy.
sentences.i: And he struck a bargain with the woman to nurse the boy.
sentences.n: ymobryn a wnaeth 'bargaining he did': the verbal noun first, closed by a wnaeth 'did' (preterite of gwneuthur), the same pattern as kyuodi a oruc. ymobryn 'hire, strike terms'. a'r wreic: a 'with' + 'r 'the'; wreic ← gwreic, softened after the article. ueithryn ← meithryn 'rear, nurse', softened because words stand between the verbal noun and it.

sentences.t: Y mab a uagwyt y ulwydyn honno.
sentences.l: The boy it-was-that was-reared that year.
sentences.i: The boy was reared through that year.
sentences.n: a uagwyt 'was reared': uagwyt ← magwyt, the impersonal preterite (-wyt) of magu, softened after a. The impersonal names no doer, 'one reared'. y ulwydyn honno 'that year': blwydyn softened after the article (feminine); honno is the feminine 'that'.

sentences.t: Ac yn oet y ulwydyn hof oed gantunt y ureisket bei dwy ulwyd.
sentences.l: And at the-age of the year, pleasing it-was with-them his stoutness were-it two years.
sentences.i: And at a year old, his size would have pleased them in a child of two.
sentences.n: yn oet y ulwydyn 'at the age of the year', at a year old. hof: so written twice in this paragraph, with a single f for hoff 'dear, pleasing' (the Red Book has hoff both times); hof oed gantunt 'it was pleasing with them', they would think it fine. The construction is clear in outline, but the exact force of hof here ('pleasing', 'marvellous'?) is not certain. gantunt 'with them', gan conjugated (3 pl.). y ureisket ← breisket 'stoutness, bigness' (from breisc 'stout'), softened after y 'his'. bei 'were it', the imperfect subjunctive of bot, used for 'if it were'. dwy ulwyd 'two years (of age)': blwyd softened after dwy, the feminine 'two'.

sentences.t: A'r eil ulwydyn mab mawr oed, ac yn gallu e hun kyrchu y llys.
sentences.l: And the second year a-boy big he-was, and able himself to-make-for the court.
sentences.i: And in the second year he was a big boy, able to make his own way to the court.
sentences.n: eil 'second' softens the noun after it: ulwydyn ← blwydyn. mab mawr oed 'a big boy he was': the predicate first, then oed, with no particle. e hun 'himself': e for y, modern ei hun. kyrchu 'make for'.

sentences.t: Ynteu e hun Wydyon, wedy y dyuot y'r llys a synnywys arnaw.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part himself Gwydion, after his coming to the court, it-was-that took-notice of-him.
sentences.i: Gwydion himself, once the boy came to the court, took notice of him.
sentences.n: Ynteu e hun Wydyon 'he himself, Gwydion': the name stands in apposition and is softened (Gwydyon > Wydyon). wedy (gwedy) 'after'; y dyuot 'his coming', the boy's. y'r 'to the'. a synnywys 'took notice': synnywys, 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of synnyaw 'perceive, take notice of' (later synnu 'wonder'). The long subject is closed by a before the verb. arnaw 'of him', literally 'on him', ar conjugated (3 sg. masc.).

sentences.t: A'r mab a ymgeneuinawd ac ef, ac a'y carawd yn uwy noc un dyn.
sentences.l: And the boy it-was-that grew-familiar with him, and that loved-him more than any man.
sentences.i: And the boy grew used to him, and loved him more than anyone.
sentences.n: a ymgeneuinawd 'grew familiar': 3 sg. preterite (-awd) of ymgyneuinaw 'become accustomed to' (kyneuin 'familiar', with e for y), with the reflexive ym-. ac ef 'with him'. a'y carawd 'loved him': the infixed 'y 'him' after a, which leaves carawd unsoftened here (as a'y kymerth in the last part); carawd, preterite (-awd) of caru. yn uwy 'more': mwy softened after yn. noc 'than' (no before a consonant). un dyn 'any one person'.

sentences.t: Yna y magwyt y mab yn y llys yny uu pedeirblwyd.
sentences.l: Then it-was the boy was-reared in the court until he-was four-years-old.
sentences.i: Then the boy was brought up at the court until he was four years old.
sentences.n: Yna y magwyt 'then was reared': the adverb first, then the particle y and the verb (the impersonal preterite, unsoftened after y). yny uu 'until he was': uu ← bu, softened after yny. pedeirblwyd 'four years old': pedeir, the feminine 'four', + blwyd.

sentences.t: A hof oed y uab wyth mlwyd uot yn gyuareisket ac ef.
sentences.l: And pleasing it-was for a-boy eight years being as-big as he.
sentences.i: And a boy of eight would have been glad to be as big as he was.
sentences.n: hof again (for hoff 'pleasing'). y uab 'for a boy': mab softened after y 'to, for'. wyth mlwyd: blwyd with the nasal mutation after wyth. uot ← bot, softened as the subject of hof oed, standing after the words between. yn gyuareisket 'as stout': so Evans prints it, certainly; the Red Book has yn gyureiscet. The form is odd: the equative of breisc 'stout', 'as stout as', is expected (kyureisket, softened after yn), and the extra -a- is not explained; it is kept as printed, and the sense 'as big as' is plain from the context. ac ef 'as he': a/ac follows an equative.

sentences.t: A diwyrnawt ef a gerdawd yn ol Gwydyon y orymdeith allan.
sentences.l: And one-day he it-was-that walked after Gwydion to walk out.
sentences.i: And one day he followed Gwydion out for a walk.
sentences.n: diwyrnawt 'one day', so spelled here. ef 'he' is the boy. a gerdawd ← kerdawd 'walked', 3 sg. preterite (-awd) of kerdet, softened after a. yn ol 'after, behind'. y orymdeith 'to walk': gorymdeith 'a walk, a going about', softened after y 'to'. allan 'out'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth, kyrchu Caer Aranrot a'r mab y gyt ac ef.
sentences.l: That-is what he-did: making-for Caer Aranrhod and the boy together with him.
sentences.i: He made for Caer Aranrhod, with the boy along with him.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth 'what he did', answered by kyrchu 'making for'; the subject is now Gwydion. Caer Aranrot is Caer Aranrhod, 'Aranrhod's fort' (r for rh, t = /d/). y gyt ac ef 'together with him'.

sentences.t: Gwedy y dyuot y'r llys, kyuodi a oruc Aranrot yn y erbyn y raessawu, ac y gyuarch guell idaw.
sentences.l: After his coming to the court, rising she-did Aranrhod against-him to welcome-him, and to greet him.
sentences.i: When he reached the court, Aranrhod rose to meet him, to welcome him and greet him.
sentences.n: kyuodi a oruc Aranrot 'rising did Aranrhod': the verbal noun first, closed by a oruc (oruc is the preterite of gwneuthur with its g dropped after a), and the subject after; a oruc serves for any person. It means simply 'she rose'. yn y erbyn 'against him', to meet him. y raessawu 'to welcome him': graessawu softened, after y 'to' or y 'his' (both soften). y gyuarch ← kyuarch 'greet', softened after y 'to'; kyuarch guell 'wish well', greet. idaw 'to him', y conjugated (3 sg. masc.).

sentences.t: “Duw a ro da it,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “God may-he-give good to-you,” said he.
sentences.i: “God give you good,” he said.
sentences.n: heb ef 'said he': heb is a defective verb used only in this tag. ro 'may give', the present subjunctive of rodi, making a wish. it 'to you', y conjugated (2 sg.). The usual answer to a greeting.

sentences.t: “Pa uab yssyd y'th ol di?” heb hi.
sentences.l: “What boy is-it-that-is in your track you?” said she.
sentences.i: “What boy is this following you?” she said.
sentences.n: Pa uab: mab softened after pa 'what'. yssyd 'that is', the relative form of bot. y'th ol 'in your track', behind you: y 'in' + 'th 'your' + ol 'track'. Evans prints yth ol (Red Book ythol); the second witness's i'th is not followed. di 'you', repeating the possessive.

sentences.t: “Y mab hwnn, mab y ti yw,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “This boy, a-son to you he-is,” said he.
sentences.i: “This boy is a son of yours,” he said.
sentences.n: mab y ti 'a son to you', your son. yw 'is'. He names her as the boy's mother.

sentences.t: “Oy a wr, ba doi arnat ti, uyg kywilydaw i, a dilyt uyg kywilyd, a'y gadw yn gyhyt a hynn?”
sentences.l: “Oh man, what came upon you, my shaming I, and pursuing my shame, and its keeping as long as this?”
sentences.i: “Oh, man, what possessed you, to shame me, and to pursue my shame, and to keep it up so long as this?”
sentences.n: Her answer, with no tag. Oy a wr 'Oh man': Oy as in Oy a Duw 'Oh God'; wr ← gwr after the vocative a. ba 'what' is pa written softened, as often. doi, a form of dyuot 'come', taken as the imperfect (as kystal y doi y gof in an earlier part): 'what was coming upon you'. The form is rare and the tense not quite certain (the Red Book has the same, pa doi). arnat 'on you', ar conjugated (2 sg.). uyg kywilydaw i 'my shaming', to shame me: the object as a possessive before the verbal noun; uyg is uy 'my' with the nasal mutation written on it, the k left plain. dilyt 'pursue, prolong' (dilyn). a'y gadw 'and its keeping': cadw softened after 'y 'its'. yn gyhyt a hynn 'as long as this': kyhyt, the equative of hir, softened after yn.

sentences.t: “Ony byd arnat ti gywilyd uwy no meithryn o honaf i uab kystal a hwnn, ys bychan a beth uyd dy gywilyd di.”
sentences.l: “If there-will-not-be on-you shame greater than rearing by me a-boy as-good as this-one, it-is small a thing that will-be your shame you.”
sentences.i: “If you have no greater shame than my rearing a boy as fine as this, your shame will be a small one.”
sentences.n: Gwydion's answer, with no tag. Ony 'if not'. byd 'will be', the present-future of bot. gywilyd ← kywilyd 'shame', softened as the subject after byd arnat ti. meithryn o honaf i 'rearing by me': the doer of the verbal noun is marked with o, here conjugated (honaf, 1 sg., written o honaf). uab ← mab, softened as its object. kystal a 'as good as', the equative of da. ys 'it is', fronting bychan 'small'. ys bychan a beth 'it is a small thing': the a beth idiom of the first part (ys glut a beth, ys iawn a beth), with beth ← peth softened; the Red Book has the same. uyd ← byd, softened after the relative a: 'a small thing that your shame will be'.

sentences.t: “Pwy enw dy uab dy?” heb hi.
sentences.l: “What name your son you?” said she.
sentences.i: “What is your son's name?” she said.
sentences.n: Pwy enw 'who (is the) name', what is the name: no verb is needed. dy uab ← mab, softened after dy 'your'. The second dy is the pronoun di 'you', written dy, repeating the possessive.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb ef, “nit oes arnaw un enw etwa.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said he, “there-is-not on-him one name yet.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” he said, “he has no name as yet.”
sentences.n: Dioer 'assuredly'. nit oes 'there is not'. arnaw 'on him': a name, like age or shame, is 'on' a person. un 'any'. etwa 'yet' (eto).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hi, “mi a dynghaf dyghet idaw, na chaffo enw yny caffo y genhyf i.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she, “I it-is-that swear a-destiny to-him, that he-may-not-get a-name until he-gets from me I.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “then I swear a destiny on him: that he shall have no name until he has it from me.”
sentences.n: a dynghaf ← tynghaf 'I swear', 1 sg. present of tyngu, softened after a. dyghet ← tynghet 'destiny, fate', softened as the object; so written here, without the n (dynghet in col. 100). To swear a tynghet on someone is to lay on them a binding fate, the thread of this part. na chaffo ← caffo, 3 sg. present subjunctive of caffael 'get', spirant after na. yny caffo 'until he gets (it)'. y genhyf i 'from me': y gan 'from (a person)', gan conjugated (1 sg.).

sentences.t: “Dygaf y Duw uyg kyffes,” heb ef, “direit wreic wyt, a'r mab a geiff enw, kyt boet drwc genhyt ti.
sentences.l: “I-bear to God my confession,” said he, “a-wicked woman you-are, and the boy it-is-that will-get a-name, though it-be bad with-you you.
sentences.i: “I make my confession to God,” he said, “you are a wicked woman, and the boy shall have a name, however little you like it.
sentences.n: Dygaf y Duw uyg kyffes, an oath, 'I bear (to) God my confession': dygaf is 1 sg. present of dwyn 'bear, bring' (or perhaps a form of tyngu 'swear'; which is not certain); the sense, a solemn oath, is plain. The same oath is in part 011, rendered the same way. uyg kyffes 'my confession', nasal written on uy, the k left plain. direit wreic wyt 'a wicked woman you are': the predicate first; direit 'wicked, ill-natured, perverse'; wreic ← gwreic, softened after the adjective standing before it. a geiff ← keiff 'will get', 3 sg. present of caffael, softened after a. kyt boet 'though it be': boet, present subjunctive of bot after kyt. drwc genhyt 'bad with you', displeasing to you; genhyt, gan conjugated (2 sg.).

sentences.t: A thitheu,” heb ef, “yr hwnn yd wyt ti, ac auar arnat am na'th elwir y uorwyn, ni'th elwir bellach byth yn uorwyn.”
sentences.l: And you-for-your-part,” said he, “that which you-are you, and grief on-you because you-are-not-called the maiden, you-will-not-be-called henceforth ever a-maiden.”
sentences.i: And as for you,” he said, “whatever you are, and for all your grief at not being called a maiden, you shall never again be called a maiden.”
sentences.n: A thitheu ← titheu 'you for your part', spirant after a. yr hwnn yd wyt ti 'that which you are': the syntax of these words is not clear; they seem to mean 'as for what you are', though yr may be the preposition 'for, in spite of' (as in yr hynny 'for all that'): 'for all that you are grieving'. The Red Book has the same words. auar 'grief, sorrow'. am 'because'. na'th elwir 'you are not called': na 'not' + 'th, the infixed object 'you' + gelwir, the impersonal present (-ir) of galw, softened after 'th. y uorwyn: morwyn softened after the article, 'the maiden', almost a title; or y may be written for yn, as in yn uorwyn at the end (the Red Book has yn uorwyn here). bellach 'henceforth', byth 'ever'. He refers to her failed test before Math at the end of the last part.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny, kerdet e ymdeith drwy y lit a wnaeth, a chyrchu Caer Tathyl, ac yno y bu y nos honno.
sentences.l: And on that, walking away through his anger he-did, and making-for Caer Dathyl, and there he-was that night.
sentences.i: At that he went off in his anger and made for Caer Dathyl, and there he spent the night.
sentences.n: kerdet e ymdeith … a wnaeth 'walking away he did': e ymdeith is y ymdeith 'away' (ymaith). drwy y lit 'through his anger': lit ← llit 'anger', softened after y 'his'. a chyrchu ← kyrchu, spirant after a. Caer Tathyl: T as in the last part; Caer Dathyl. yno y bu 'there he was': he spent the night.

sentences.t: A thrannoeth kyuodi a oruc, a chymryt y uab gyt ac ef, a mynet y orymdeith gan lann y weilgi rwng hynny ac Aber Menei.
sentences.l: And next-day rising he-did, and taking his boy with him, and going to walk along the-shore of the sea between that and Aber Menai.
sentences.i: The next day he rose, took the boy with him, and went walking along the seashore between there and Aber Menai.
sentences.n: A thrannoeth ← trannoeth 'next day', spirant after a. kyuodi a oruc, then the verbal nouns a chymryt (kymryt, spirant after a) and a mynet carry the narrative on. y uab ← mab, softened after y 'his'. y orymdeith 'to walk', as before. gan lann 'along the shore': glann softened after gan. y weilgi ← gweilgi 'sea, ocean', softened after the article. rwng hynny ac 'between that (place) and'. Aber Menei is Aber Menai, the mouth of the Menai.

sentences.t: Ac yn y lle y guelas delysc a morwyal, hudaw llong a wnaeth.
sentences.l: And in the place that he-saw dulse and sea-wrack, conjuring a-ship he-did.
sentences.i: And at a spot where he saw dulse and sea-wrack, he made a ship by magic.
sentences.n: yn y lle y guelas 'in the place where he saw': guelas, 3 sg. preterite (-as) of gwelet. delysc 'dulse', an edible red seaweed (modern dylysg). morwyal: a seaweed, perhaps a kind of kelp or wrack; which plant is meant is not certain. hudaw llong a wnaeth 'conjuring a ship he did': hudaw 'make by magic' (hut 'magic').

sentences.t: Ac o'r guimon a'r delysc hudaw cordwal a wnaeth, a hynny llawer, ac eu brithaw a oruc hyt na welsei neb lledyr degach noc ef.
sentences.l: And from the wrack and the dulse conjuring cordwain he-did, and that much, and their colouring he-did so-that no-one had-seen leather fairer than it.
sentences.i: And out of the wrack and the dulse he made cordwain by magic, plenty of it, and coloured it so finely that no one had ever seen fairer leather.
sentences.n: o'r 'from the'. guimon 'seaweed, wrack' (gwymon). cordwal 'cordwain', fine leather (the name from Cordova). a hynny llawer 'and that much', plenty of it. eu brithaw 'their speckling': eu 'their' (no mutation), the object before the verbal noun; brithaw (from brith 'speckled') is to colour or pattern; what exactly is done to the leather is not certain. hyt na 'so that not'. welsei ← gwelsei 'had seen', the pluperfect (-sei) of gwelet, softened after na. degach ← tegach 'fairer', comparative of teg, softened after its noun although lledyr is masculine; such softening of an adjective after a masculine noun is found in Middle Welsh, but irregularly. noc ef 'than it'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny, kyweiraw hwyl ar y llong a wnaeth, a dyuot y drws porth Caer Aranrot, ef a'r mab yn y llong.
sentences.l: And on that, rigging a-sail on the ship he-did, and coming to the door of-the-gate of Caer Aranrhod, he and the boy in the ship.
sentences.i: Then he rigged a sail on the ship and came to the entrance of Caer Aranrhod, he and the boy in the ship.
sentences.n: kyweiraw 'prepare, rig'. hwyl 'sail'. y drws 'to the door': y 'to'. porth is 'gate' or 'landing-place, harbour'; drws porth is the gateway of the fort, which here stands by the water. ef a'r mab 'he and the boy'.

sentences.t: Ac yna dechreu llunyaw esgidyeu, ac eu gwniaw.
sentences.l: And then beginning shaping shoes, and their sewing.
sentences.i: And then he began to cut out shoes and stitch them.
sentences.n: dechreu 'beginning': the verbal nouns stand on their own, with no a oruc to close them and no person named. llunyaw 'shape, fashion' (llun 'form'). esgidyeu 'shoes', plural of esgid. eu gwniaw 'their sewing', stitching them.

sentences.t: Ac yna y harganuot o'r gaer.
sentences.l: And then their being-sighted from the fort.
sentences.i: And then they were sighted from the fort.
sentences.n: y harganuot 'their sighting': y is eu 'their' (written y), and the h- before the vowel shows it; arganuot 'catch sight of'. The possessive before the verbal noun is its object: 'they were sighted'. o'r gaer ← caer, softened after the article (feminine).

sentences.t: Pan wybu ynteu y arganuot o'r gaer, dwy eu heilyw e hun a oruc, a dodi eilyw arall arnunt, ual nat adnepit.
sentences.l: When knew he-for-his-part his being-sighted from the fort, taking their colour own he-did, and putting colour other on-them, so-that one-might-not-recognise.
sentences.i: When he knew that he had been sighted from the fort, he took away their own looks and put other looks on them, so that they would not be known.
sentences.n: Pan wybu 'when knew': wybu ← gwybu, preterite of gwybot, softened after Pan. y arganuot 'his being sighted': no h- here, so y is 'his' (the Red Book has eu harganuot 'their'). dwy: so the White Book, with no n, plainly on the image: a scribal slip for dwyn 'take away' (Red Book dôyn; the second witness silently prints dwyn). It is kept as written and read as dwyn. eu heilyw 'their colour, their appearance': eu 'their' puts h- before a vowel; eilyw 'colour, hue, looks'. e hun 'own'. a oruc closes dwy(n) … ; a dodi 'and putting' follows. arnunt 'on them', ar conjugated (3 pl.). ual nat 'so that not'. adnepit 'one would recognise', the impersonal imperfect (-it) of adnabot.

sentences.t: “Pa dynyon yssyd yn y llong?” heb yr Aranrot.
sentences.l: “What men is-it-that-are in the ship?” said Aranrhod.
sentences.i: “What men are those in the ship?” said Aranrhod.
sentences.n: dynyon 'people, men', plural of dyn. yssyd 'that are', the relative form of bot, which serves for plural too. heb yr Aranrot 'said Aranrhod': heb y(r) before a name.

sentences.t: “Crydyon,” heb wy.
sentences.l: “Shoemakers,” said they.
sentences.i: “Shoemakers,” they said.
sentences.n: Crydyon, plural of cryd 'shoemaker' (crydd). heb wy 'said they': wy 'they'.

sentences.t: “Ewch y edrych pa ryw ledyr yssyd ganthunt, a pha ryw weith a wnant.”
sentences.l: “Go to look what kind of-leather is-there with-them, and what kind of-work they-do.”
sentences.i: “Go and see what sort of leather they have, and what sort of work they do.”
sentences.n: Ewch 'go', 2 pl. imperative of mynet. y edrych 'to look'. pa ryw 'what kind of': ryw softens what follows, ledyr ← lledyr 'leather', weith ← gweith 'work'. ganthunt 'with them', gan conjugated (3 pl.), spelled with th here, gantunt elsewhere. a pha ← pa, spirant after a. a wnant 'they do', 3 pl. present of gwneuthur.

sentences.t: Yna y doethpwyt, a phan doethpwyt, yd oed ef yn brithaw cordwal, a hynny yn eureit.
sentences.l: Then there-was-coming, and when there-was-coming, he-was colouring cordwain, and that golden.
sentences.i: So they went, and when they got there, he was colouring cordwain, and doing it in gold.
sentences.n: y doethpwyt 'there was coming': doethpwyt, the impersonal preterite of dyuot, names no one; the messengers are meant. a phan ← pan, spirant after a. yd oed ef yn brithaw 'he was colouring'. eureit 'golden, gilded' (eur 'gold'); a hynny yn eureit 'and that golden', in gold.

sentences.t: Yna y doeth y kennadeu, a menegi idi hi hynny.
sentences.l: Then came the messengers, and telling to-her she that.
sentences.i: Then the messengers came back and told her of it.
sentences.n: y doeth 'came': the verb is singular because its plural subject, y kennadeu 'the messengers' (plural of kennat), follows it. menegi 'telling, reporting'. idi 'to her', y conjugated (3 sg. fem.).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hitheu, “dygwch uessur uyn troet, ac erchwch y'r cryd wneuthur esgidyeu im.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she-for-her-part, “take the-measure of-my foot, and ask to the shoemaker making shoes for-me.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “take the measure of my foot, and ask the shoemaker to make me shoes.”
sentences.n: hitheu 'she for her part'. dygwch 'take, bring', 2 pl. imperative of dwyn. uessur ← messur 'measure', softened as the object. uyn troet 'my foot': uyn is uy 'my' with the nasal written on it; troet is not written changed. erchwch 'ask', 2 pl. imperative of erchi. y'r cryd 'to the shoemaker'. wneuthur ← gwneuthur, softened because words stand between it and the verb. im 'for me'.

sentences.t: Ynteu a lunywys yr esgidyeu, ac nit wrth y messur, namyn yn uwy.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part it-was-that shaped the shoes, and not by the measure, but larger.
sentences.i: He made the shoes, but not to the measure: larger.
sentences.n: a lunywys ← llunywys 'shaped', 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of llunyaw, softened after a. wrth y messur 'by the measure'. namyn 'but, except'. yn uwy 'larger': mwy softened after yn.

sentences.t: Dyuot a'r esgidyeu idi.
sentences.l: Coming with the shoes to-her.
sentences.i: The shoes were brought to her.
sentences.n: Dyuot a 'coming with', bringing: a verbal noun with no person named.

sentences.t: Nachaf yr esgidyeu yn ormod.
sentences.l: Behold the shoes too-big.
sentences.i: And see, the shoes were too big.
sentences.n: Nachaf 'behold, lo' (like llyma), with no verb after it. yn ormod ← gormod 'too much', softened after yn.

sentences.t: “Ryuawr yw y rei hynn,” heb hi.
sentences.l: “Too-big are these ones,” said she.
sentences.i: “These are too big,” she said.
sentences.n: Ryuawr 'too big': ry- 'too' + mawr, softened in the compound. yw 'is': the singular verb before a plural subject. y rei hynn 'these ones': rei 'ones'.

sentences.t: “Ef a geiff werth y rei hynn, a gwnaet heuyt rei a uo llei noc wynt.”
sentences.l: “He it-is-that will-get the-price of these ones, and let-him-make also ones that may-be smaller than they.”
sentences.i: “He shall have the price of these, and let him make others smaller than these.”
sentences.n: Still Aranrhod; the tag is in the unit before. a geiff ← keiff 'will get', 3 sg. present of caffael, softened after a. werth ← gwerth 'price', softened as the object. gwnaet 'let him make', 3 sg. imperative of gwneuthur. heuyt 'also'. a uo 'that may be': uo ← bo, present subjunctive of bot, softened after a. llei 'smaller'. noc wynt 'than they'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ef, gwneuthur rei ereill yn llei lawer no'y throet, a'y hanuon idi.
sentences.l: That-is what he-did he: making ones other smaller by-much than her foot, and their sending to-her.
sentences.i: What he did was make another pair much smaller than her foot, and send them to her.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth ef, answered by the verbal nouns. rei ereill 'other ones'. lawer ← llawer 'much', softened as an adverb. no'y throet 'than her foot': no 'than' + 'y 'her', which gives the spirant mutation, troet > throet; that is how the reader knows it is 'her'. a'y hanuon 'and their sending': here 'y is 'their', putting h- before anuon 'send'.

sentences.t: “Dywedwch idaw, nit a ymi un o'r esgidyeu hynn,” heb hi.
sentences.l: “Tell to-him, there-goes-not to-me one of these shoes,” said she.
sentences.i: “Tell him that not one of these shoes will go on me,” she said.
sentences.n: Dywedwch 'tell', 2 pl. imperative of dywedut. nit a 'does not go': a 'goes', 3 sg. present of mynet. ymi 'to me', y conjugated (1 sg.): the shoes will not go on her. un 'one'.

sentences.t: Ef a dywetpwyt idaw.
sentences.l: It it-was-that was-said to-him.
sentences.i: This was told him.
sentences.n: Ef here is not 'he' but an empty 'it' that lets the sentence begin with a pronoun before a. dywetpwyt 'was said', the impersonal preterite of dywedut. idaw 'to him'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ef, “ny lunyaf esgidyeu idi yny welhwyf y throet.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he, “I-will-not-shape shoes for-her until I-see her foot.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “I will make no shoes for her until I see her foot.”
sentences.n: ny lunyaf ← llunyaf 'I will shape', 1 sg. present-future, softened after ny. idi 'for her'. yny welhwyf 'until I see': welhwyf ← gwelhwyf, 1 sg. present subjunctive of gwelet (with -h-), softened after yny. y throet 'her foot': spirant after 'her' again.

sentences.t: A hynny a dywetpwyt idi.
sentences.l: And that it-was-that was-said to-her.
sentences.i: And that was told her.
sentences.n: The same frame as two sentences back, with hynny 'that' as the subject.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hi, “mi a af hyt attaw.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she, “I it-is-that will-go as-far-as to-him.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “I will go to him.”
sentences.n: a af 'will go', 1 sg. present of mynet. hyt attaw 'as far as to him', right up to him: attaw, at conjugated (3 sg. masc.).

sentences.t: Ac yna y doeth hi hyt y llong.
sentences.l: And then came she as-far-as the ship.
sentences.i: And then she came down to the ship.
sentences.n: y doeth hi 'she came', with the particle y after yna. hyt 'as far as'.

sentences.t: A phan doeth, yd oed ef yn llunyaw, a'r mab yn gwniaw.
sentences.l: And when she-came, he-was shaping, and the boy sewing.
sentences.i: And when she came, he was cutting shoes and the boy was stitching.
sentences.n: A phan ← pan, spirant after a. yd oed ef yn llunyaw 'he was shaping'; the second clause borrows the verb: a'r mab yn gwniaw 'and the boy (was) sewing'.

sentences.t: “Ie, Arglwydes,” heb ef, “dyd da it.”
sentences.l: “Yes, Lady,” said he, “day good to-you.”
sentences.i: “Yes, Lady,” he said, “good day to you.”
sentences.n: Arglwydes 'lady' (arglwyd 'lord' + -es). dyd da it 'good day to you', as in the last part.

sentences.t: “Duw a ro da it,” heb hi.
sentences.l: “God may-he-give good to-you,” said she.
sentences.i: “God give you good,” she said.
sentences.n: The same answer to a greeting as Gwydion gave her: ro, the present subjunctive of rodi.

sentences.t: “Eres yw genhyf na uedrut kymedroli esgidyeu wrth uessur.”
sentences.l: “Strange it-is with-me that you-could-not moderate shoes by measure.”
sentences.i: “I find it strange that you could not make shoes to a measure.”
sentences.n: Eres yw genhyf 'strange it is with me', I find it strange: genhyf, gan conjugated (1 sg.). na uedrut 'that you could not': uedrut ← medrut, 2 sg. imperfect of medru 'be able, know how', softened after na. kymedroli 'make moderate, fit to size' (kymedrawl 'moderate'). The White Book has no words missing here: the Red Book reads gymedroli ar wneuthur esgidyeu 'manage the making of shoes', and the second witness prints [ar wneuthur] from it, but nothing is supplied, since the White Book's 'moderate shoes to a measure' reads as it stands. wrth uessur 'by measure': messur softened after wrth.

sentences.t: “Na uedreis,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “I-could-not,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “I could not,” he said.
sentences.n: Na uedreis 'I could not': uedreis ← medreis, 1 sg. preterite (-eis) of medru, softened after na. Welsh answers by repeating the verb, here with the negative na.

sentences.t: “Mi a'y medraf weithon.”
sentences.l: “I it-is-that it will-manage now.”
sentences.i: “I shall manage it now.”
sentences.n: Still Gwydion. a'y 'it', the infixed object after a, with medraf 'I will manage', 1 sg. present-future, unsoftened (as a'y carawd above). weithon 'now'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny, llyma y dryw yn seuyll ar wwrd y llog.
sentences.l: And on that, behold the wren standing on the board of the ship.
sentences.i: And at that moment, there was a wren perched on the ship's deck.
sentences.n: llyma 'behold, here is' puts the scene before your eyes. y dryw 'the wren'. yn seuyll 'standing'. ar wwrd 'on the board, the deck': bwrd softened after ar, the softened sound /v/ written w (so too y wwyta in col. 98); the Red Book has ar vŵrd. llog: so written, a slip for llong 'ship' (Red Book yllong), kept as written.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth y mab, y uwrw a'y uedru y rwg giewyn y esgeir a'r ascwrn.
sentences.l: That-is what the boy did: its casting-at and its hitting between the sinew of its leg and the bone.
sentences.i: The boy took aim at it and struck it between the sinew of its leg and the bone.
sentences.n: y uwrw 'its throwing', throwing at it: bwrw softened after y 'its'. a'y uedru 'and its hitting': medru, the verb of 'be able' above, here in its root sense 'hit (a mark)', softened after 'y 'its'. y rwg: so written, for y rwng 'between' (the n not written), kept. giewyn 'sinew' (gewyn). y esgeir 'its leg, its shank'. ascwrn 'bone' (asgwrn).

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth hitheu, chwerthin.
sentences.l: That-is what she-did she-for-her-part: laughing.
sentences.i: And she laughed.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth hitheu, answered by the one verbal noun chwerthin 'laughing'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb hi, “ys llaw gyffes y medrwys y Lleu ef.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said she, “it-is with-a-hand steady that hit the Fair-one it.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” she said, “it is with a sure hand that the fair one has hit it.”
sentences.n: ys 'it is', fronting llaw gyffes 'a steady hand': gyffes ← kyffes, softened after llaw (feminine). The adjective is taken to mean 'sure, deft, steady'; whether it is the same word as kyffes 'confession' in col. 95 is uncertain. y medrwys 'that hit': medrwys, 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of medru. y Lleu 'the fair one, the bright one': lleu 'light, bright' used as a noun. Her words give the boy his name. ef 'it', the wren; ef could also repeat the subject ('the fair one, he'), but 'it' is the likelier. The Red Book has the same words.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “aniolwch Duw it.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “un-thanks of-God to-you.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “and God give you no thanks for it.
sentences.n: aniolwch 'unthanks, ill will': an- 'not' + diolwch 'thanks', the d swallowed by the n of an-. Duw 'of God'. it 'to you'. It is a curse in form, or close to 'no thanks to you'; she named him without meaning to.

sentences.t: Neur gauas ef enw.
sentences.l: Indeed-has got he a-name.
sentences.i: He has got a name now.
sentences.n: Neur is the particle neu 'indeed' + ry, which makes the preterite a perfect: 'he has got'. gauas ← kauas, preterite of caffael, softened after neur. Evans prints a false start, an n dotted beneath (the scribe's cancellation), before enw; it is left out.

sentences.t: A da digawn yw y enw.
sentences.l: And good enough is his name.
sentences.i: And a good enough name it is.
sentences.n: da digawn 'good enough', the predicate first. y enw 'his name'.

sentences.t: Llew Llaw Gyffes yw bellach.”
sentences.l: Lleu Hand Steady he-is henceforth.”
sentences.i: Lleu Llaw Gyffes he is from now on.”
sentences.n: Llew: so written here, with the 6-shaped w (and below), though y Lleu above has u; both are kept as Evans prints them. The name is Lleu Llaw Gyffes, 'Lleu of the Steady Hand'. The spelling Llew could be read as llew 'lion', but the naming plays on lleu 'bright'. yw 'is'. bellach 'from now on'.

sentences.t: Ac yna difflannu y gueith yn delysc ac yn wimon.
sentences.l: And then vanishing the work into dulse and into wrack.
sentences.i: And then the work vanished back into dulse and wrack.
sentences.n: difflannu 'vanishing' (diflannu), a verbal noun with no a oruc. y gueith 'the work': unsoftened after the article, so this is the masculine gweith 'work', not the feminine gweith 'time' of weithon. yn delysc, yn wimon 'into dulse, into wrack': gwimon softened after yn. This is the predicative yn ('becoming, as'), which softens; the preposition yn 'in' would give the nasal mutation.

sentences.t: A'r gueith ny chanlynwys ef hwy no hynny.
sentences.l: And the work he-did-not-follow he longer than that.
sentences.i: And he did not keep at that craft any longer.
sentences.n: A'r gueith 'and the work', the object put first. ny chanlynwys 'did not follow': canlynwys, 3 sg. preterite of canlyn, spirant after ny. hwy 'longer', comparative of hir. no hynny 'than that'.

sentences.t: Ac o'r achaws hwnnw y gelwit ef yn drydyd eur gryd.
sentences.l: And for that reason he-was-called a-third gold-shoemaker.
sentences.i: And for that reason he was called one of the Three Golden Shoemakers.
sentences.n: o'r achaws hwnnw 'for that cause'. y gelwit 'he was called': gelwit, the impersonal imperfect (-it) of galw. yn drydyd ← trydyd 'third', softened after yn. eur gryd 'gold shoemaker': cryd softened after eur in the compound. The triad formula again: 'the third', one of a set of three; the other two are not named here.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb hitheu, “ni henbydy well di o uot yn drwc wrthyf i.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said she-for-her-part, “you-will-not-fare better you from being bad towards me.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” she said, “you will be none the better for treating me badly.”
sentences.n: Aranrhod speaks; the paragraph returns to the scene at the ship. ni henbydy 'you will not fare': henbydy, 2 sg. present-future of hanbot 'be, come of, fare'. well ← gwell 'better', softened as the complement. o uot 'from being': bot softened after o. wrthyf 'towards me', wrth conjugated (1 sg.).

sentences.t: “Ny buum drwc i etwa wrthyt ti,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I-have-not-been bad I yet towards you you,” said he.
sentences.i: “I have not been bad to you yet,” he said.
sentences.n: Ny buum 'I have not been', 1 sg. preterite of bot. etwa 'yet'. wrthyt 'towards you', wrth conjugated (2 sg.).

sentences.t: Ac yna yd ellyngwys ef y uab yn y bryt e hun, ac y kymerth y furyf e hun.
sentences.l: And then he-released he his boy into his form own, and he-took his shape own.
sentences.i: And then he released the boy into his own form, and took his own shape again.
sentences.n: yd ellyngwys 'released': 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of ellwng, the form of gollwng without g (as i ellwng in the first part). y uab ← mab after y 'his'. yn y bryt e hun 'into his own form': bryt ← pryt 'form, looks', softened after y 'his' (as dy bryt 'your looks' in an earlier part; pryt is a different word from bryt 'mind'). The Red Book has yny b[r]yt ehun too, and lacks the second clause. y kymerth 'he took'. y furyf 'his form': furyf is ffuryf 'shape', with a single f, as in hof.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hitheu, “minheu a dyghaf dyghet y'r mab hwnn, na chaffo arueu byth yny gwiscof i ymdanaw.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she-for-her-part, “I-for-my-part it-is-that swear a-destiny to this boy, that he-may-not-get arms ever until I-dress I about-him.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “and I swear a destiny on this boy: that he shall never have arms until I put them on him myself.”
sentences.n: minheu 'I for my part'. a dyghaf … dyghet, written without the n again (tynghaf, tynghet, softened). na chaffo arueu 'that he may not get arms': arueu 'arms, weapons'. yny gwiscof 'until I dress': gwiscof, 1 sg. present subjunctive of gwiscaw 'put on, dress', with -of beside the usual ending -wyf (the Red Book has gwisgwyf); after yny one expects the softened wiscof, but the g stands, in the Red Book as well. ymdanaw 'about him', ymdan conjugated (3 sg. masc.). Evans prints a mark like ! after heb hitheu at the line end; it is not a letter and nothing is missing.

sentences.t: “Y rof a Duw,” heb ef, “handid o'th direidi di, ac ef a geif arueu.”
sentences.l: “Between me and God,” said he, “let-it-come of your wickedness you, and he it-is-that will-get arms.”
sentences.i: “Between me and God,” he said, “let your wickedness come to what it will, he shall have arms.”
sentences.n: Y rof a Duw 'between me and God' (rof 'between me'), written without i. handid, 3 sg. present subjunctive of hanbot 'be, come of'; handid o'th direidi 'may it come of your wickedness'. The exact force is uncertain: perhaps 'it will be your wickedness's doing', perhaps 'for all your wickedness'. direidi 'wickedness, perversity' (from direit). o'th 'of your'. a geif 'will get': keif, written with one f here, softened after a.

sentences.t: Yna y doethant wy parth a Dinas Dinllef.
sentences.l: Then came they towards Dinas Dinlle.
sentences.i: Then they went towards Dinas Dinlle.
sentences.n: y doethant 'they came', 3 pl. preterite of dyuot. parth a 'towards'. Dinllef: so written, with a final f; the place is Dinas Dinlle on the coast of Arfon.

sentences.t: Ac yna meithryn Llew Llaw Gyffes yny allwys marchogaeth pob march, ac yny oed gwbyl o bryt, a thwf, a meint.
sentences.l: And then rearing Lleu Llaw Gyffes until he-could ride every horse, and until he-was complete of form, and growth, and size.
sentences.i: And there Lleu Llaw Gyffes was reared until he could ride any horse, and was full grown in looks and stature and size.
sentences.n: meithryn 'rearing', a verbal noun with no doer named. Llew: the w spelling again. yny allwys 'until he could': allwys ← gallwys, 3 sg. preterite of gallu, softened after yny. marchogaeth 'ride'. gwbyl ← cwbyl 'complete, whole', softened as the predicate after oed. o bryt ← pryt 'form, looks', softened after o. a thwf ← twf 'growth', spirant after a. meint 'size'. Evans prints a / after pob; it is a mark, not a letter, and is not printed.

sentences.t: Ac yna adnabot a wnaeth Gwydyon arnaw y uot yn kymryt dihirwch o eisseu meirch ac arueu, a'y alw attaw a wnaeth.
sentences.l: And then recognising did Gwydion on-him his being taking listlessness from lack of-horses and arms, and his calling to-him he-did.
sentences.i: And then Gwydion saw that the lad was growing listless for want of horses and arms, and he called him to him.
sentences.n: adnabot a wnaeth Gwydyon 'recognising did Gwydion': the verbal noun first, the subject after a wnaeth. adnabot … arnaw 'recognise on him', see in him. y uot 'his being': bot softened after y 'his'. yn kymryt 'taking': yn before a verbal noun causes no mutation. dihirwch: 'listlessness, dejection' is the sense the context asks for; the word's range (sloth, wretchedness) makes the exact shade uncertain. o eisseu 'for want of'. meirch 'horses', plural of march. a'y alw 'and his calling': galw softened after 'y 'his'. attaw 'to him'. Evans prints a mark like ! after eisseu at the line end; it is not a letter and nothing is missing.

sentences.t: “A was,” heb ynteu, “ni a awn, ui a thi, y neges auory.
sentences.l: “O lad,” said he-for-his-part, “we it-is-that will-go, I and you, on an-errand tomorrow.
sentences.i: “Lad,” he said, “we shall go, you and I, on an errand tomorrow.
sentences.n: A was ← gwas 'lad', softened after the vocative a. a awn 'will go', 1 pl. present of mynet. ui a thi 'I and you': ui is mi softened, a thi spirant after a. y neges 'on an errand': y 'to'. auory 'tomorrow'.

sentences.t: A byd lawenach noc yd wyt.”
sentences.l: And be more-cheerful than you-are.”
sentences.i: And be more cheerful than you are.”
sentences.n: byd 'be', 2 sg. imperative of bot. lawenach ← llawenach, comparative of llawen 'glad', softened as the complement. noc yd wyt 'than you are'.

sentences.t: “A hynny a wnaf inheu,” heb y guas.
sentences.l: “And that I-for-my-part it-is-that will-do,” said the lad.
sentences.i: “That I will,” said the lad.
sentences.n: hynny 'that', the object put first. a wnaf 'I will do', 1 sg. present of gwneuthur. inheu 'I for my part'. heb y guas 'said the lad'.

sentences.t: Ac yn ieuengtit y dyd trannoeth, kyuodi a wnaethant, a chymryt yr aruordir y uynyd parth a Brynn Aryen.
sentences.l: And in the youth of the day next-day, rising they-did, and taking the coastland upwards towards Bryn Arien.
sentences.i: And early the next morning they rose and went up along the coastland towards Bryn Arien.
sentences.n: yn ieuengtit y dyd 'in the youth of the day', early morning, as in the first part. kyuodi a wnaethant 'rising they did': a wnaethant, 3 pl. preterite of gwneuthur. a chymryt ← kymryt, spirant after a. aruordir 'coastland' (ar 'by' + mor 'sea' + tir 'land'). y uynyd 'upwards': mynyd softened after y. parth a 'towards'. Brynn Aryen: Bryn Arien, a hill; where exactly it was is not certain.

sentences.t: Ac yn y penn uchaf y Geuyn Clutno, ymgueiraw ar ueirch a wnaethant, a dyuot parth a Chaer Aranrot.
sentences.l: And at the end highest of Cefn Clydno, equipping-themselves with horses they-did, and coming towards Caer Aranrhod.
sentences.i: And at the top of Cefn Clydno they fitted themselves out with horses, and came on towards Caer Aranrhod.
sentences.n: y penn uchaf 'the highest end', the top. y Geuyn: keuyn 'ridge' softened after the preposition y 'to', here 'of'; it is not the article, after which the masculine keuyn would not soften. Geuyn Clutno is Cefn Clydno. ymgueiraw ar ueirch 'equip themselves on horses': ymgueiraw is ym- + kyweiraw 'prepare'; ueirch ← meirch, softened after ar. a Chaer ← Caer, spirant after a.

sentences.t: Ac yna amgenu eu pryt a wnaethant, a chyrchu y porth yn rith deu was ieueinc, eithyr y uot yn prudach pryt Gwydyon noc un y guas.
sentences.l: And then changing their form they-did, and making-for the gate in-the-guise of two lads young, except its being graver the-face of-Gwydion than that of the lad.
sentences.i: And then they changed their looks and made for the gate in the guise of two young men, except that Gwydion's face was graver than the lad's.
sentences.n: amgenu 'change' (amgen 'other'). eu pryt 'their form, their looks'. yn rith 'in the guise of'. deu was ← gwas, softened after deu. ieueinc, plural of ieuanc 'young'. eithyr 'except'. y uot 'its being': bot softened after y. prudach 'graver, more sober', comparative of prud; after the predicative yn one expects the softened brudach, but the p stands (the Red Book has yn prudach too). noc un y guas 'than the one of the lad', than the lad's (face).

sentences.t: “E porthawr,” heb ef, “dos ymywn, a dywet uot yma beird o Uorgannwc.”
sentences.l: “O porter,” said he, “go in, and say there-being here bards from Morgannwg.”
sentences.i: “Porter,” he said, “go in and say that there are poets here from Morgannwg.”
sentences.n: E porthawr 'O porter': E for the vocative a. dos 'go', 2 sg. imperative of mynet. ymywn 'in'. dywet 'say', 2 sg. imperative. uot ← bot, softened as the object of dywet: 'that there are'. beird 'poets, bards', plural of bard. o Uorgannwc ← Morgannwc, softened after o: Morgannwg, Glamorgan in the south.

sentences.t: Y porthawr a aeth.
sentences.l: The porter it-was-that went.
sentences.i: The porter went.
sentences.n: a aeth 'went', 3 sg. preterite of mynet.

sentences.t: “Graessaw Duw wrthunt.
sentences.l: “The-welcome of-God towards-them.
sentences.i: “God's welcome to them.
sentences.n: Aranrhod speaks; the tag is in the next unit. Graessaw 'welcome'. wrthunt 'towards them', wrth conjugated (3 pl.).

sentences.t: Gellwng y mywn wy,” heb hi.
sentences.l: Let in them,” said she.
sentences.i: Let them in,” she said.
sentences.n: Gellwng 'let go, let', 2 sg. imperative. y mywn 'in', written apart here (ymywn above). wy 'them'.

sentences.t: Diruawr leuenyd a uu yn eu herbyn.
sentences.l: Very-great joy it-was-that was against-them.
sentences.i: They were met with great rejoicing.
sentences.n: Diruawr 'huge, very great': di-, strengthening, + mawr softened. leuenyd ← llewenyd 'joy', softened after the adjective standing before it. a uu 'was'. yn eu herbyn 'against them', to meet them: eu puts h- before erbyn.

sentences.t: Yr yneuad a gyweirwyd ac y wwyta yd aethpwyt.
sentences.l: The hall it-was-that was-prepared and to eating there-was-going.
sentences.i: The hall was made ready, and they went to eat.
sentences.n: yneuad 'hall' (neuad). a gyweirwyd 'was prepared': kyweirwyd, the impersonal preterite of kyweiraw, softened after a. y wwyta 'to eat': bwyta softened after y 'to', the /v/ written w as in ar wwrd. yd aethpwyt 'there was going': aethpwyt, the impersonal preterite of mynet.

sentences.t: Guedy daruot y bwyta, ymdidan a wnaeth hi a Guydyon am chwedleu a chyuarwydyt.
sentences.l: After finishing the eating, conversing she-did with Gwydion about tales and storytelling.
sentences.i: When the meal was over, she talked with Gwydion of tales and storytelling.
sentences.n: Guedy daruot 'after finishing': daruot 'end, be done'. y bwyta 'the eating'. ymdidan a wnaeth hi 'conversing she did'. a Guydyon 'with Gwydion'. chwedleu 'tales'. a chyuarwydyt ← kyuarwydyt, spirant after a: 'storytelling, lore', the art of the kyuarwyd. Evans prints a mark like ! after Guydyon at the line end; it is not a letter and nothing is missing.

sentences.t: Ynteu Wydyon kyuarwyd da oed.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Gwydion a-storyteller good he-was.
sentences.i: Gwydion was a fine storyteller.
sentences.n: Ynteu Wydyon: the name softened after ynteu, as Ynteu e hun Wydyon in col. 94, and as Ynteu Wydyon in part 011. kyuarwyd 'storyteller' (also 'guide, one who knows the way'), with da 'good', the predicate first, then oed.

sentences.t: Guedy bot yn amser ymadaw a chyuedach, ystauell a gweirwyt udunt wy, ac y gyscu yd aethant.
sentences.l: After being time to-leave off carousal, a-chamber it-was-that was-prepared for-them they, and to sleep they-went.
sentences.i: When it was time to leave the drinking, a chamber was made ready for them, and they went to sleep.
sentences.n: bot yn amser 'its being time'. ymadaw a 'leave, part from'. chyuedach ← kyuedach 'carousal, drinking together', spirant after a. ystauell 'chamber'. a gweirwyt 'was prepared': for gyweirwyt ← kyweirwyt, the impersonal preterite of kyweiraw, softened after a, with the y of the first syllable not written (compare a gyweirwyd above; the Red Book has a gyweirwyt). udunt 'for them', y conjugated (3 pl.). y gyscu 'to sleep': kyscu softened after y 'to'. yd aethant 'they went'.

sentences.t: Hir bylgeint Guydyon a gyuodes.
sentences.l: Long before-dawn Gwydion it-was-that rose.
sentences.i: Well before dawn Gwydion rose.
sentences.n: Hir bylgeint 'long (in the) dawn-time': pylgeint is the early hours before daybreak, softened after hir 'long', an adjective standing before its noun; the phrase, an adverb of time, means 'deep in the small hours'. a gyuodes ← kyuodes 'rose', 3 sg. preterite (-es) of kyuodi.

sentences.t: Ac yna y gelwis ef y hut a'y allu attaw.
sentences.l: And then he-called he his magic and his power to-him.
sentences.i: And then he called up his magic and his power.
sentences.n: y gelwis 'he called', 3 sg. preterite (-is) of galw. hut 'magic'. a'y allu 'and his power': gallu softened after 'y 'his'. attaw 'to him'.

sentences.t: Erbyn pan oed y dyd yn goleuhau, yd oed gyniweir ac utkyrn a lleuein yn y wlat yn gynghan.
sentences.l: By when the day was brightening, there-was a-host-astir and trumpets and shouting in the land in-concert.
sentences.i: By the time day was breaking, there was a stir of troops, and trumpets and shouting through all the land together.
sentences.n: Erbyn pan 'by when', by the time that. y dyd: Evans prints the y raised above the line, brought into it here (the Red Book has pan oed y dyd). goleuhau 'grow light'. yd oed 'there was'. gyniweir ← kyniweir, softened after oed: 'a host, a coming and going of armed men'; the meaning is not quite certain, and the print is faint, read on the image at high zoom (Red Book geniweir), so the reading is slightly uncertain too. utkyrn 'trumpets', plural of utkorn. lleuein 'shouting, crying'. y wlat ← gwlat, softened after the article. yn gynghan ← kynghan 'in concert, all together', softened after the adverbial yn.

sentences.t: Pan ydoed y dyd yn dyuot, wynt a glywynt taraw drws yr ystauell, ac ar hynny Aranrot yn erchi agori.
sentences.l: When was the day coming, they it-was-that heard striking on the door of the chamber, and on that Aranrhod asking to-open.
sentences.i: As the day came on, they heard a knocking at the chamber door, and with it Aranrhod asking them to open.
sentences.n: ydoed is yd oed, written as one word. a glywynt 'heard', 3 pl. imperfect of clywet, softened after a. taraw 'striking', knocking. yn erchi 'asking'. agori 'opening'.

sentences.t: Kyuodi a oruc y guas ieuanc, ac agori.
sentences.l: Rising did the young lad, and opening.
sentences.i: The young lad rose and opened.
sentences.n: kyuodi a oruc with its subject y guas ieuanc after it; ac agori 'and opening' follows. The young lad is Lleu.

sentences.t: Hitheu a doeth y mywn, a morwyn y gyt a hi.
sentences.l: She-for-her-part it-was-that came in, and a-maiden together with her.
sentences.i: She came in, and a maiden with her.
sentences.n: Hitheu 'she for her part'. y mywn 'in'. y gyt a hi 'together with her'.

sentences.t: “A wyrda,” heb hi, “lle drwc yd ym.”
sentences.l: “O noblemen,” said she, “a-place bad it-is we-are.”
sentences.i: “Noblemen,” she said, “we are in a bad place.”
sentences.n: A wyrda ← gwyrda 'noblemen' (gwyr + da), softened after the vocative a. lle drwc 'a bad place', put first, then yd ym 'we are', 1 pl. present of bot.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “ni a glywn utkyrn a lleuein, a beth a debygy di o hynny?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “we it-is-that hear trumpets and shouting, and what do-you-think you of that?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “we hear trumpets and shouting; what do you make of it?”
sentences.n: a glywn 'we hear', 1 pl. present of clywet, softened after a. beth ← peth 'thing', used for 'what'. a debygy ← tebygy 'you think', 2 sg. present of tebygu, softened after a.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb hi, “ni chawn welet llyw y weilgi gan pob llong ar torr y gilyd.
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said she, “we-cannot-get to-see the-colour of the sea for every ship on the-belly of its fellow.
sentences.i: “Indeed,” she said, “we cannot see the colour of the sea for ships, each one pressed against the next.
sentences.n: ni chawn welet 'we cannot get to see': cawn, 1 pl. present of cael, spirant after ni; welet ← gwelet, softened as the object of chawn. llyw: read as lliw 'colour' (y for i); llyw is also 'rudder, ruler', but the sense needs 'colour', and the Red Book has lliw; llyw is certain on the image, so it is kept and read as lliw. y weilgi ← gweilgi 'sea', softened after the article. gan 'because of'; pob is not softened after it here (the Red Book has gan bop). ar torr y gilyd 'on the belly of its fellow', each against the next: torr 'belly, bulge'; y gilyd 'its fellow' (modern ei gilydd).

sentences.t: Ac y maent yn kyrchu y tir yn gyntaf a allont.
sentences.l: And they-are making-for the land as-soon as they-can.
sentences.i: And they are making for the shore as fast as they can.
sentences.n: y maent 'they are', 3 pl. present of bot. yn kyrchu 'making for'. yn gyntaf a allont 'as first as they can', as fast as they can: kyntaf, the superlative of kynt, softened after yn; a allont, 3 pl. present subjunctive of gallu, softened after a.

sentences.t: A pha beth a wnawn i?” heb hi.
sentences.l: And what thing will-we-do we?” said she.
sentences.i: And what shall we do?” she said.
sentences.n: a pha ← pa, spirant after a; pa beth 'what thing', what. a wnawn 'shall we do', 1 pl. present of gwneuthur, softened after a. i: Evans prints wnawn i with a space; it stands for wnawn ni, the n of the pronoun absorbed into the n before it (Red Book awnawn ni).

sentences.t: “Arglwydes,” heb y Gwydyon, “nyt oes in gynghor, onyt caeu y gaer arnam, a'y chynhal yn oreu a allom.”
sentences.l: “Lady,” said Gwydion, “there-is-not to-us counsel, except closing the fort on-us, and its holding as best as we-can.”
sentences.i: “Lady,” said Gwydion, “there is nothing for it but to shut the fort on ourselves and hold it as best we can.”
sentences.n: nyt oes in gynghor 'there is no counsel for us': in 'to us'; gynghor ← kynghor, softened as the subject after nyt oes in. onyt 'except'. caeu 'closing'. y gaer ← caer. arnam 'on us', ar conjugated (1 pl.). a'y chynhal 'and its holding': kynhal 'hold, maintain', spirant after 'y 'her' (caer is feminine). yn oreu ← goreu 'best', softened after yn. a allom 'we can', 1 pl. present subjunctive of gallu.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hitheu, “Duw a dalho ywch.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she-for-her-part, “God may-he-repay to-you.
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “may God repay you.
sentences.n: Duw a dalho ywch, the house formula with talho for talo: the present subjunctive of talu with -h-, softened after a. ywch 'to you', y conjugated (2 pl.).

sentences.t: A chynhelwch chwitheu; ac yma y keffwch digawn o arueu.”
sentences.l: And hold you-for-your-part; and here you-will-get enough of arms.”
sentences.i: Hold it, then; and here you will find arms enough.”
sentences.n: chynhelwch ← kynhelwch 'hold', 2 pl. imperative of kynhal (the a changed to e before the ending), spirant after a. chwitheu 'you for your part'. y keffwch 'you will get', 2 pl. present-future of caffael. digawn o 'enough of'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny, yn ol yr arueu yd aeth hi.
sentences.l: And on that, after the arms it-was she-went.
sentences.i: And with that she went to fetch the arms.
sentences.n: yn ol yr arueu 'after the arms', to fetch them, put first, then yd and the verb. aeth 'went'.

sentences.t: A llyma hi yn dyuot, a dwy uorwyn gyt a hi, ac arueu deu wr gantunt.
sentences.l: And behold she coming, and two maidens with her, and the-arms of-two men with-them.
sentences.i: And here she came, with two maidens, and the arms for two men between them.
sentences.n: llyma hi yn dyuot 'behold her coming'. dwy uorwyn ← morwyn, softened after dwy, the feminine 'two', with the noun singular after the numeral. deu wr ← gwr, softened after deu. gantunt 'with them'.

sentences.t: “Arglwydes,” heb ef, “gwisc ymdan y gwryanc hwnn.
sentences.l: “Lady,” said he, “dress about this young-man.
sentences.i: “Lady,” he said, “arm this young man.
sentences.n: gwisc 'dress, put on', 2 sg. imperative of gwiscaw. ymdan 'about'. gwryanc 'young man' (gwr + ieuanc).

sentences.t: A minheu, ui a'r morynyon, a wiscaf ymdanaf inheu.
sentences.l: And I-for-my-part, I and the maidens, it-is-that will-dress about-me I-for-my-part.
sentences.i: And I will arm myself, with the maidens' help.
sentences.n: A minheu 'and I for my part'. ui a'r morynyon 'I and the maidens': ui is mi softened; morynyon, plural of morwyn. a wiscaf ← gwiscaf 'I will dress', softened after a. ymdanaf 'about me', ymdan conjugated (1 sg.). inheu again 'I for my part'.

sentences.t: Mi a glywaf odorun y gwyr yn dyuot.”
sentences.l: I it-is-that hear the-din of the men coming.”
sentences.i: I can hear the noise of the men coming.”
sentences.n: a glywaf 'I hear'. odorun ← godorun 'din, uproar', softened as the object, as in the last part.

sentences.t: “Hynny a wnaf yn llawen.”
sentences.l: “That I-will-do gladly.”
sentences.i: “That I will do gladly.”
sentences.n: Aranrhod's answer, with no tag. hynny 'that', the object first. yn llawen 'gladly'.

sentences.t: A guiscaw a wnaeth hi amdanaw ef yn llawen, ac yn gwbyl.
sentences.l: And dressing she-did about-him he gladly, and completely.
sentences.i: And she armed him gladly and completely.
sentences.n: guiscaw a wnaeth hi 'dressing she did'. amdanaw 'about him', another spelling of ymdanaw. yn gwbyl 'completely': gwbyl ← cwbyl (cwbl), softened after the adverbial yn; the Red Book has yn gwbyl too. yn llawen beside it shows no change, since ll is not softened after yn.

sentences.t: “A derw,” heb ef, “wiscaw amdan y gwryanc hwnnw?”
sentences.l: “Has-it-ended,” said he, “dressing about that young-man?”
sentences.i: “Is it done,” he said, “the arming of that young man?”
sentences.n: A, the question particle. derw: so written, for deryw 'has ended', the perfect (3 sg.) of daruot; the answer has Deryw. It is kept as written. wiscaw ← gwiscaw, softened as the subject after the verb.

sentences.t: “Deryw,” heb hi.
sentences.l: “It-has-ended,” said she.
sentences.i: “It is,” she said.
sentences.n: Deryw 'it has ended': the answer repeats the verb of the question.

sentences.t: “Neu deryw y minheu,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Indeed it-has-ended to me-for-my-part,” said he.
sentences.i: “And mine is done too,” he said.
sentences.n: Neu 'indeed', the affirmative particle (as in neur). y minheu 'to me for my part'.

sentences.t: “Diodwn yn arueu weithon; nit reit ynn wrthunt.”
sentences.l: “Let-us-take-off our arms now; there-is-not need to-us of-them.”
sentences.i: “Let us take off our arms now; we have no need of them.”
sentences.n: Diodwn 'let us take off', 1 pl. imperative of diodi (di- + dodi). yn arueu 'our arms': yn is the possessive 'our' (modern ein), which usually puts h- before a vowel (Red Book an harueu); here none is written. weithon 'now'. nit reit 'there is no need': reit 'need'. ynn 'to us'. wrthunt 'of them': reit wrth is 'need of'.

sentences.t: “Och,” heb hitheu, “paham?
sentences.l: “Och,” said she-for-her-part, “why?
sentences.i: “Oh,” she said, “why?
sentences.n: Och 'oh'. paham 'why' (pa 'what' + am 'for').

sentences.t: Llyna y llynghes yng kylch y ty.”
sentences.l: There-is the fleet around the house.”
sentences.i: There is the fleet all round the house.”
sentences.n: Llyna 'there is, see there', the partner of llyma. llynghes 'fleet'. yng kylch 'around': yn + kylch 'circle', the nasal written ng and the k left plain.

sentences.t: “A wreic, nit oes yna un llynghes.”
sentences.l: “O woman, there-is-not there any fleet.”
sentences.i: “Woman, there is no fleet there.”
sentences.n: Gwydion answers, with no tag. A wreic ← gwreic, softened after the vocative a. nit oes 'there is not'. un 'any'.

sentences.t: “Och,” heb, “pa ryw dygyuor a uu o honei?”
sentences.l: “Och,” said, “what kind of mustering was there of-it?”
sentences.i: “Oh,” she said, “then what sort of muster was that?”
sentences.n: heb stands here with no subject: Evans prints Och heb. pa ryw with no blank. The second witness supplies [hi] and the Red Book has heb hitheu; nothing is supplied, since the speaker is plain from the dialogue (compare 'heb mab Mathonwy' in the last part). pa ryw 'what kind of'. dygyuor 'mustering, a hosting' (as in the last part). a uu 'was'. o honei 'of it': o conjugated (3 sg. fem.), probably referring to the llynghes (feminine); the exact force is not certain.

sentences.t: “Dygyuor,” heb ynteu, “y dorri dy dynghetuen am dy uab, ac y geissaw arueu idaw.
sentences.l: “A-mustering,” said he-for-his-part, “to break your destiny about your son, and to seek arms for-him.
sentences.i: “A muster,” he said, “to break the destiny you swore on your son, and to get arms for him.
sentences.n: y dorri ← torri 'break', softened after y 'to'. dy dynghetuen ← tynghetuen 'destiny' (tynghet + -uen), softened after dy. dy uab ← mab. y geissaw ← keissaw 'seek', softened after y. idaw 'for him'.

sentences.t: Ac neur gauas ef arueu, heb y diolwch y ti.”
sentences.l: And indeed-has got he arms, without the thanks to you.”
sentences.i: And he has got arms, and no thanks to you.”
sentences.n: Ac neur: ac is written before a consonant here. neur gauas 'has got', as with the name. heb y diolwch y ti 'without the thanks to you': diolwch 'thanks'.

sentences.t: “E rof a Duw,” heb hitheu, “gwr drwc wyt ti.
sentences.l: “Between me and God,” said she-for-her-part, “a-man bad you-are you.
sentences.i: “Between me and God,” she said, “you are a wicked man.
sentences.n: E rof a Duw: Evans prints Erof, E for Y as in Y rof a Duw above. gwr drwc 'a bad man', the predicate first, then wyt 'you are'.

sentences.t: Ac ef a allei llawer mab colli y eneit am y dygyuor a bereisti yn y cantref hwnn hediw.
sentences.l: And it it-was-that could many a-son lose his life for the mustering that you-caused in this cantref today.
sentences.i: And many a son might have lost his life over the muster you raised in this cantref today.
sentences.n: ef 'it', the empty subject again. a allei 'could', the imperfect of gallu (gallei, softened after a), here 'might have'. llawer mab 'many a son': llawer takes a singular noun. colli 'lose'. y eneit 'his life': eneit is 'soul' and 'life'. am 'for, over'. a bereisti 'that you caused': pereist, 2 sg. preterite (-eist) of peri, with ti joined on, softened after a. hediw 'today'.

sentences.t: A mi a dynghaf dynghet idaw,” heb hi, “na chaffo wreic uyth, o'r genedyl yssyd ar y dayar honn yr awr honn.”
sentences.l: And I it-is-that swear a-destiny to-him,” said she, “that he-may-not-get a-wife ever, of the race that-is on this earth this hour.”
sentences.i: And I swear a destiny on him,” she said, “that he shall never have a wife of the race that is on this earth now.”
sentences.n: a dynghaf dynghet, with the n written this time. na chaffo 'that he may not get', as before. wreic ← gwreic, softened as the object. uyth ← byth 'ever', softened as an adverb. o'r genedyl 'of the race': kenedyl 'kindred, people', softened after the article (feminine). yssyd 'that is'. y dayar honn 'this earth'. yr awr honn 'this hour', now.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “direidwreic uuost eiroet, ac ny dylyei neb uot yn borth it.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “a-wicked-woman you-have-been ever, and ought-not anyone to-be a support to-you.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “a wicked woman you have always been, and no one ought to stand by you.
sentences.n: direidwreic 'wicked woman': direit + gwreic, softened in the compound, the predicate first. uuost ← buost 'you have been', 2 sg. preterite of bot, softened after the fronted predicate. eiroet 'ever'. ny dylyei 'ought not', imperfect of dylyu. neb 'anyone'. uot ← bot, softened as the object of dylyei, after neb. yn borth ← porth 'support, help', softened after yn. it 'to you'.

sentences.t: A gwreic a geif ef ual kynt.”
sentences.l: And a-wife it-is-that will-get he as before.”
sentences.i: And he shall have a wife all the same.”
sentences.n: gwreic 'a wife', the object first. a geif 'will get' (keif, one f, softened after a). ual kynt 'as before': as with the name and the arms.

sentences.t: Hwynteu a doethant at Math uab Mathonwy, a chwynaw yn luttaf yn y byt rac Aranrot a wnaethant, a menegi ual y paryssei yr arueu idaw oll.
sentences.l: They-for-their-part it-was-that came to Math son of-Mathonwy, and complaining most-vehemently in the world against Aranrhod they-did, and telling how he-had-caused the arms to-him all.
sentences.i: They went to Math son of Mathonwy and made the bitterest complaint in the world against Aranrhod, and told him the whole of how the arms had been got for the lad.
sentences.n: Hwynteu is wynteu 'they for their part', written with h. a doethant 'came', 3 pl. preterite of dyuot. uab ← mab, softened after the name. a chwynaw ← cwynaw 'complain', spirant after a; a wnaethant closes it. yn luttaf: lluttaf, superlative of llut 'eager, vehement', softened after yn; 'most vehemently', though the precise sense of llut is uncertain. yn y byt 'in the world'. rac 'against'. menegi 'telling'. y paryssei 'had caused': the pluperfect (-yssei) of peri, 'how (he) had caused (to be got) the arms for him'; the subject is unexpressed, most likely Gwydion. oll 'all'. Evans prints a stray ' before arueu; it is a mark, not a letter, and is not printed.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Math, “keisswn inheu, ui a thi, oc an hut a'n lledrith, hudaw gwreic idaw ynteu o'r blodeu.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Math, “let-us-seek we-for-our-part, I and you, from our magic and our enchantment, to-conjure a-wife for-him he-for-his-part from the flowers.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Math, “let us try, you and I, by our magic and enchantment, to conjure a wife for him out of flowers.”
sentences.n: keisswn 'let us seek, let us try', 1 pl. imperative of keissaw. inheu: so Evans (the second witness ninheu, Red Book ninneu), for ninheu 'we for our part', the n lost against the n before it, as with wnawn i; kept as printed. ui a thi 'I and you'. oc an hut 'from our magic': oc is o before a vowel; an 'our'. a'n lledrith 'and our enchantment': 'n 'our'; lledrith 'illusion, enchantment'. hudaw 'conjure'. idaw ynteu 'for him'. o'r blodeu 'from the flowers'.

sentences.t: Ynteu yna a meint gwr yndaw ac yn delediwhaf guas a welas dyn eiroet.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part then with the-size of-a-man in-him and the most-handsome lad that a-person saw ever.
sentences.i: He by then had a man's full size in him, and was the handsomest lad anyone ever saw.
sentences.n: A sentence with no verb: Ynteu yna 'he then (was)'. a meint gwr yndaw 'with a man's size in him': yndaw 'in him', yn conjugated (3 sg. masc.). yn delediwhaf ← telediwhaf 'most handsome', superlative of telediw, softened after yn. a welas dyn 'that anyone saw': welas ← gwelas, softened after a; dyn 'a person'. eiroet 'ever'.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kymeryssant wy blodeu y deri, a blodeu y banadyl, a blodeu yr erwein, ac o'r rei hynny, asswynaw yr un uorwyn deccaf a thelediwaf a welas dyn eiroet.
sentences.l: And then they-took they the-flowers of the oaks, and the-flowers of the broom, and the-flowers of the meadowsweet, and from those ones, conjuring the one maiden fairest and most-handsome that a-person saw ever.
sentences.i: And then they took the flowers of the oak, and the flowers of the broom, and the flowers of the meadowsweet, and out of these they conjured up the fairest and loveliest maiden anyone ever saw.
sentences.n: y kymeryssant 'they took', 3 pl. preterite of kymryt. deri 'oaks', plural of derw. banadyl 'broom'. erwein 'meadowsweet'. o'r rei hynny 'from those ones'. asswynaw 'invoke, conjure'. yr un uorwyn deccaf 'the one fairest maiden', the very fairest: uorwyn ← morwyn, softened after un (feminine); deccaf, superlative of teg. a thelediwaf ← telediwaf, spirant after a.

sentences.t: Ac y bedydyaw o'r bedyd a wneynt yna, a dodi Blodeued arnei.
sentences.l: And her baptising with the baptism that they-used-to-make then, and putting Blodeuedd on-her.
sentences.i: And they baptised her with the baptism they used in those days, and gave her the name Blodeuedd.
sentences.n: y bedydyaw 'her baptising': y 'her' gives no soft mutation, so bedydyaw stands. o'r bedyd 'with the baptism'. a wneynt 'that they used to make', 3 pl. imperfect of gwneuthur. yna 'then', the narrator's 'in those days'. dodi … arnei 'putting on her', naming her: arnei, ar conjugated (3 sg. fem.). Blodeued is Blodeuedd (d = /ð/; Red Book blodeuwed), from blodeu 'flowers'.

sentences.t: Gwedy y kyscu y gyt wy ar y wled, “Nyt hawd,” heb y Guydyon, “y wr heb gyuoeth idaw ossymdeithawc.”
sentences.l: After their sleeping together they at the feast, “Not easy,” said Gwydion, “for a-man without a-realm of-his-own provided.”
sentences.i: After they had slept together at the feast, “It is not easy,” said Gwydion, “for a man without a realm of his own to make his way.”
sentences.n: Gwedy y kyscu 'after their sleeping': y is eu 'their', so kyscu is unsoftened. y gyt 'together'. ar y wled 'at the feast': gwled softened after the article (feminine). Nyt hawd 'not easy'. y wr ← gwr, softened after y 'for'. heb gyuoeth ← kyuoeth 'realm', softened after heb. idaw 'of his own'. ossymdeithawc: so Evans, the final c certain on the image; the second witness and the Red Book have ossymdeithaw, a verbal noun 'to make provision, get a living'. Evans's form looks like an adjective in -awc ('provided for, with means to live'?), perhaps on ossymdeith 'provision, livelihood'; the reading is kept, and its meaning is uncertain. Evans prints a suspension stroke over the y of y gyt; nothing is missing, and it is not printed.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Math, “mi a rodaf idaw yr un cantref goreu y was ieuanc y gael.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Math, “I it-is-that will-give to-him the one cantref best for a-lad young to get.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Math, “I will give him the one cantref that is best for a young man to have.”
sentences.n: a rodaf 'I will give', 1 sg. present-future of rodi. yr un cantref goreu 'the one best cantref'. y was ← gwas, softened after y 'for'. y gael ← cael, softened after y 'to'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb ef, “pa gantref yw hwnnw?”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said he, “what cantref is that?”
sentences.i: “Lord,” he said, “which cantref is that?”
sentences.n: pa gantref ← cantref, softened after pa.

sentences.t: “Cantref Dinodig,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Cantref Dunoding,” said he.
sentences.i: “The cantref of Dunoding,” he said.
sentences.n: Dinodig is the cantref known as Dunoding, in the west of Gwynedd.

sentences.t: A hwnnw a elwir yr awr honn Eiwynyd ac Ardudwy.
sentences.l: And that it-is-that is-called this hour Eifionydd and Ardudwy.
sentences.i: And that is now called Eifionydd and Ardudwy.
sentences.n: a elwir 'is called': gelwir, the impersonal present (-ir) of galw, softened after a. yr awr honn 'this hour', the narrator's own day. Eiwynyd is Eifionydd, with w for /v/.

sentences.t: Sef lle ar y cantref y kyuanhedwys lys idaw, yn y lle a elwir Mur Castell, a hynny yg gwrthtir Ardudwy.
sentences.l: That-is the-place in the cantref that he-settled a-court for-him, in the place that is-called Mur Castell, and that in-the-uplands of-Ardudwy.
sentences.i: The place in the cantref where he set up his court was at the spot called Mur Castell, in the uplands of Ardudwy.
sentences.n: Sef lle 'that is the place', answered by yn y lle a elwir Mur Castell. ar y cantref 'in the cantref'. y kyuanhedwys 'he settled, established', 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of kyuanhedu. lys ← llys, softened as the object. idaw 'for him'. Mur Castell 'castle wall'. yg gwrthtir 'in the uplands of': Evans prints ygg6zthtir; yn + gwrthtir 'high ground', the nasal written in yg and not on the g of gwrthtir.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kyuanhedwys ef, ac y gwledychwys.
sentences.l: And then he-settled he, and he-ruled.
sentences.i: And there he settled and ruled.
sentences.n: y kyuanhedwys, again, here 'dwelt, settled'. y gwledychwys 'he ruled', 3 sg. preterite of gwledychu (gwlat 'land').

sentences.t: A phawb a uu uodlawn idaw, ac y arglwydiaeth.
sentences.l: And everyone it-was-that was content with-him, and with his lordship.
sentences.i: And everyone was content with him and with his rule.
sentences.n: A phawb ← pawb, spirant after a. a uu 'was'. uodlawn ← bodlawn 'content', softened after uu. idaw 'with him', literally 'to him'. ac y arglwydiaeth 'and to his lordship': y is 'to' and 'his' run together. The part ends at col. 101 l. 17; the next begins on the same line.
